features.description: Standalone curl installer for macOS/Linux and Windows, plus npm and Homebrew; `codex update` applies CLI self-updates when the installed release supports them.

Sign in with ChatGPT (subscription access) or an OpenAI API key (usage-based), or access tokens; `codex login` browser OAuth, `codex logout`, `codex login status`; login on headless devices supported.
Terminal UI with model/directory banner, syntax-highlighted code and diffs, a prompt composer with draft history, and image paste.
60+ built-in slash commands (/init, /status, /permissions, /model, /review, /compact, /plan, /goal, /fork, /resume …) with fuzzy filtering and Tab-queueing while a chat runs.
`codex resume` reopens the most recent chat (`--last`, `--all`) or the picker; `/resume` in-session; saved-directory prompts controlled by tui.resume_cwd.

`codex fork` / `/fork` copies a saved chat into a new one; Esc+Esc on an empty composer edits a previous user message and forks from that point; `codex exec fork <SESSION_ID>` forks non-interactively, including into a worktree.
`/rename` names the chat; `codex archive|unarchive` hides sessions without deleting transcripts (cascades to subagent sessions); `codex delete` removes them permanently.
`codex queue --thread <SESSION_ID> --message …` queues a text message into an existing session, optionally resuming it first.
`/compact` summarizes the chat to free tokens, `/recap` summarizes without compacting, and `/status` shows model, approval policy, writable roots, and remaining context.

Tab queues a follow-up for the next turn, Enter injects instructions into the current turn, `!` runs a local shell command under current approvals, `@` searches workspace files, Ctrl+O copies the last response.
`/ps` lists background terminals with recent output; `/stop` stops them all.
`/side` (alias `/btw`) opens a side chat for focused follow-ups outside the main transcript.
`/permissions` selects Read Only, Auto (workspace-write with on-request approvals), or Full Access; the desktop/IDE composer also offers Ask for approval vs Approve for me.
`--ask-for-approval` decides when Codex pauses before crossing the sandbox (on-request in the Auto preset); the retired `untrusted` policy has a documented migration path.

With approvals_reviewer = auto_review, approval requests route to a reviewer agent that approves or denies with a rationale; `/approve` retries one denial; policy configurable, incl. authorized cyber engagements.
Asynchronous monitoring can pause a task on potentially unsafe model behavior; you review findings before resuming.

Platform-native sandboxing (macOS Seatbelt, Linux sandboxing, native Windows) limits spawned commands to workspace writes and blocks network by default; `codex sandbox` runs a command under the same policy.
Elevated native Windows agent sandbox via `/setup-default-sandbox`; legacy sandbox removable with `codex sandbox uninstall`; WSL supported and documented.
Beta filesystem/network profiles in config define writable roots, network access, and sandbox settings; `--add-dir` extends writable roots without full access.
Starlark `.rules` files (e.g. ~/.codex/rules/default.rules) control which commands may run outside the sandbox, with prompt/deny decisions; `codex execpolicy check` validates rule files.
`/plan` switches to plan mode, optionally with a prompt, so Codex proposes an execution plan before implementation starts.
`/goal` sets, edits, pauses, resumes, views, or clears a persistent target Codex keeps working toward across a larger task.

Codex layers global (~/.codex/AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md) and project AGENTS.md files root-down at startup, with configurable fallback filenames, a 32KiB default cap, `/init` scaffolding, and Code Review rules sections.
Local memory files distilled from eligible prior chats, generated in the background with secret redaction; enable and configure with `/memories`; stored under $CODEX_HOME (v1/v2 stores).

hooks.json or config.toml run scripts or MCP tools on lifecycle events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, SubagentStart, Stop, session start) from system, user, and trusted-project scopes, with trust gating and managed requirements.toml hooks.

`codex mcp add` registers stdio or streamable-HTTP MCP servers (OAuth incl. CIMD/DCR, ChatGPT session auth); `/mcp` lists configured tools; server `instructions` become guidance; config shared across CLI, IDE, and desktop.
`/skills` browses and applies local skills; `$` mentions invoke them explicitly or they match by description; skills load from local directories, plugins, and curated sets, and can be disabled.
`codex plugin add|list|remove` installs plugins (skills, hooks, MCP servers, apps) from marketplaces including GitHub repos; `/plugins` browses in-session; JSON output for automation.
`/apps` browses connector apps (Gmail, Google Calendar, GitHub, Drive…) and inserts one into the prompt as $app-slug; destructive connector calls still require approval.
Ask Codex to spawn parallel subagent threads for divided work; `/subagents` inspects or switches the active subagent thread; custom agents configurable.

`/model` (or `--model`) chooses the active model and reasoning effort; recommended: GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday coding, GPT-6.2 Astra for complex projects, Luna for small automations, Terra for visual reasoning.
`/fast` toggles a faster token-generation tier (≈1.5x on supported models) for ChatGPT-signed-in CLI/IDE users; Ultrafast is faster still at higher allowance use.
`/daybreak` toggles an approved cybersecurity access program for eligible accounts and models.
Built-in web search runs cached (OpenAI-maintained index) by default; `--search` or web_search = "live" switches to live browsing; domain filters via config.
`--image` attaches screenshots or diagrams to a task; paste images into the interactive composer.

`/worktree` starts or continues a chat in a managed Git worktree; `codex fork --worktree` and `codex exec --worktree` fork into one; Handoff moves a chat between Local and Worktree; scheduled tasks run on dedicated worktrees.
Setup scripts and reusable actions configure a local project for Codex, plus built-in Git tools.

`/review` or non-interactive `codex review --uncommitted|--base|--commit|PROMPT` reviews changes with presets (PR-style against a base branch) without modifying the working tree; findings support inline comments, staging, and reverting.

Install the Codex GitHub integration, request reviews with `@codex review`, enable automatic PR reviews, and customize findings with Code Review Rules in AGENTS.md; `@codex security review` runs Security Review.
Code Review for GitLab merge requests via `@codex review`, with automatic reviews and AGENTS.md review rules (preview).
Run Codex chats from Linear issues, auto-assign issues to Codex, or connect Linear locally through MCP.
Start requests in Slack and delegate repository work to Codex Cloud.
`openai/codex-action@v1` runs codex exec in GitHub Actions workflows, applies patches, and posts reviews from CI.

`codex cloud` browses cloud chats, `codex cloud exec` submits a task directly, `codex cloud list` returns recent chats as text or JSON, and `codex apply` applies a cloud chat's diff to your local repo.
Reusable, publishable cloud environments with setup scripts, cached state, environment variables and network secrets, VPN/private networking, and OIDC access to cloud resources.
Start, guide, approve, and review Codex tasks from the ChatGPT mobile app — in the cloud or on a connected computer.
Use Codex on mobile against a connected Mac/Windows PC, connect the desktop app to projects over SSH, and hand off a chat between hosts.
The Codex VS Code extension works beside your code: open files and selections enter the prompt via `/ide`, edits review in place, and slash commands match the CLI.
`/app` or `codex app` continues the current session in the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS/Windows, which adds an integrated terminal, computer use, voice, and Codex Micro support.
Run commands and inspect output without leaving the chat; turn repeated commands into reusable actions.
Let ChatGPT/Codex use desktop apps while it works.
Limited-run Work Louder keyboard for the ChatGPT desktop app: Agent Keys switch chats, customizable Command Keys, dial and analog stick, voice input, and lighting.
`codex agents` (or `/agents`) browses chats and switches between agents on a shared server; `--remote` targets another machine's app-server.
`codex --remote ws://host:port` (or unix:// socket) runs the terminal UI against an app-server started elsewhere, with bearer-token auth.

`codex exec` runs scripted/CI tasks with pre-set sandbox and approvals; `--json` NDJSON events, `--output-schema` JSON-schema results, `--output-last-message`, stdin piping, `exec resume --last|--all`, `--ephemeral` and `--worktree` runs.
TypeScript and Python libraries start, continue, and resume local Codex threads for CI pipelines or embedding Codex in your own tools.
`codex app-server` exposes the protocol that powers the VS Code extension — threads, turns, approvals, skills, streamed events — for building custom clients; open source in openai/codex.
Automations run Codex tasks on schedules or from supported app events, with background-worktree isolation and cleanup; create from the web or by asking in a chat.
TUI notifications when a turn completes, plus an external `notify` program configured via config.toml.

`/theme` syntax-highlighting themes (custom .tmTheme), `codex completion` shell completions, Ctrl+G external editor, `/keymap` shortcut remapping, `/vim`, `/statusline` and `/title` footer fields, `/tui` scrollback vs fullscreen, `/raw` raw scrollback.
`/presets` saves and recalls frequently used prompts or slash commands.
The CLI import flow brings supported setup, projects, and recent work from Claude Code or Cursor into Codex.
On macOS, demonstrate a workflow once and Codex turns the recording into a reusable skill.
Project-scoped .codex/ config, hooks, and rules load only from trusted projects; user and system layers always load.

config.toml at system/user/project scopes sets model, sandbox, approvals, and web search; named profiles via `--profile`; feature flags managed with `codex features enable|disable` and `/experimental` (network proxy, prevent sleep).
Route local Codex surfaces to OpenAI models through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI, or custom providers via configuration.

`codex doctor` generates a local diagnostic report; `codex debug models|prompt-input` inspect the model catalog and prompt input; `/debug-config`, `/warnings`, `/export`, `/diff`, and `/feedback` (with diagnostic ZIP) round out debugging.
`/usage` shows daily, weekly, and cumulative ChatGPT token activity and rate-limit resets from inside the TUI.
Security scans of repositories and pull requests: in-session plugin scans, the Codex Security CLI with GitHub Actions/GitLab CI, findings triage, and verified patches.
The Codex CLI and app-server are open source in the openai/codex GitHub repository, with community resources documented.
